title: Tech Note: Integrating Active4D and the 4D Ajax Framework
author: Jason T. Slack, Technical Support Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note documents integrating Active4D, a third-party ASP-style scripting/web-server layer for 4D (developed by Aparajita's World, not by 4D Inc.), with 4D's own 4D Ajax Framework, by custom-routing requests in the On Web Connection method based on a '@DAX@' marker and merging both systems' web roots into a shared 'web_decoy' folder. Both halves of this integration — the third-party Active4D product and 4D's in-house 4DAF/4D Web 2.0 Pack — are long defunct, making this note a snapshot of an ecosystem-level integration technique from an early, fragmented era of 4D web development rather than a currently applicable how-to.
related_updates: Active4D, the third-party product this note depends on, is no longer an actively maintained or available product
4D Web 2.0 Pack and the 4D Ajax Framework (4DAF) have been discontinued by 4D
Modern 4D web applications are built with 4D's built-in Web Server and Qodly component tooling rather than third-party ASP-style layers or 4DAF
